dedupe_keys.name: australian mobile coverage programme datasets mobile black spot program and peri urban mobile program

description: The Australian communications department publishes open geodata for its programmes that fund new mobile base stations where the market has not provided coverage. The Mobile Black Spot Program, co-funded by state and local governments and by the mobile network operators Optus, Telstra and TPG Telecom and infrastructure providers Field Solutions Group and OneWiFi, has generated more than one billion Australian dollars of investment over rounds 1 to 7 for up to 1,400 new base stations; the dataset gives all funded base stations as a zipped download and a WMS layer, and a separate dataset maps the areas ineligible for round 8. The Peri-Urban Mobile Program funds base stations on the fringes of major cities, where high cost, difficult terrain and lower population density have left areas underserved; its round 1 dataset gives funded base stations as KML, WFS and GeoJSON, with round 2 eligible corridors in another entry. Coverage: Australia, programme rounds since 2015. Format and access: zip, KML, GeoJSON, WFS and WMS from data.gov.au, free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: sites are funded locations, some not yet built; coverage footprints of the sites are not included in these datasets. Simulation uses: coverage gaps and new sites in regional and peri-urban areas, exposure of new base stations to bushfire and flood, and redundancy planning. Related records: the Mobile Black Spot Program case study evaluates the programme, the Mobile Network Hardening Program dataset lists resilience upgrades at these sites, and the ACMA register lists all licensed transmitters.
